correctness.rationale: For every even integer dimension at least six, Fourier characters of the even-weight binary subgroup diagonalize its weight-two adjacency. The spectrum is determined exactly by \(((d-2|a|)^2-d)/2\). A normalized projector-square Fourier convolution counts precisely two events (intersection half the support or half the complement) with an explicit inclusion-exclusion overlap, yielding a nonnegative exact eigenvalue for every character. Odd-weight cosets vanish and even-weight cosets are strictly positive, proving rank \(2^{d-2}\) and the exact antipodally antisymmetric kernel. A strictly decreasing increment argument for \(1-\binom{2j}{j}/4^j\) proves the optimal positive spectral gap and its asymptotic. The standard-library exact verifier independently checks direct adjacency eigenfunctions, projectors, Fourier spectrum, parity kernel and finite binomial counts; these finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: Even halved cubes are a natural infinite distance-regular family known to admit perfect state transfer. Determining the exact antipodal nullspace, proving no extra rank defect, computing the full positive Fourier spectrum, and finding the sharp nonzero eigenvalue quantifies mode survival under time averaging, a motivated transport invariant. The theorem is neither a restatement of PST nor an arbitrary low-dimensional computation; it is a complete infinite-family classification with a quantitative gap.
